suites.title: guest access through the HTTPS origin

specs.title: Welcome -> Join -> Pre-Join -> meeting over HTTPS; the guest cookie is Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict
direct URL and WebSocket bypass attempts fail: no session, wrong-meeting session, and a passcode field on the socket
five failures lock the meeting; the lock is stored in PostgreSQL and survives a MAIN container restart; the host can lift it
the DEPLOYED application role is append-only on security events (effective privileges, inherited ones included) and the passcode never reaches the database
the recovery allowance used BEFORE a MAIN restart is still counted AFTER it: two lifts, restart, exactly one more succeeds, concurrent requests cannot exceed it

suites.title: Meet through the single HTTPS origin (/meet/)

specs.title: Meet UI loads under /meet/, redirects /meet, and its assets and API are prefix-aware
internal bridge, recovery and readiness endpoints are not reachable even with the right secret header
two browsers meet under /meet/: websocket upgrade on the prefixed path, chat both ways, passcode, refresh and rejoin

suites.title: AI Meeting Intelligence - meeting to report in the browser

specs.title: host consents, builds a report from the real Meet chat, assigns work, shares, exports, and revokes - with permissions enforced throughout
plan limit: the Basic plan allows 3 AI reports a month and the dashboard explains it
every internal link on the pricing page, the portal and the apps menu resolves (no dead product/sidebar links)
[I07] header and product links on the pricing page are same-origin routes to the portal
[I08][I09] sidebar items work from the keyboard and open real portal pages
apps menu opens, items are reachable by Tab, and Escape closes it and restores focus
highlights expand/collapse by mouse and keyboard
phone layout: pricing and portal pages do not overflow horizontally and purchase controls stay reachable
tablet layout: pricing and portal pages do not overflow horizontally and purchase controls stay reachable
legacy pages keep working: /index.html (built-in meetings), /chat.html, /qorlla.html, /login.html
[I01][I02][I03] the catalogue is same-origin only: no CORS grants, GET-only, private endpoints closed
the phone page states that telephony is off, shows an empty history, and public webhooks refuse to run
receptionist: create a profile, set business hours, enable it, add rules, and book an appointment against the hours
the workspace owner sees the manager-only phone sections

suites.title: portal - real MAIN sign-in, workspaces, authorization

specs.title: signed-out visitors get a sign-in prompt on private pages and the API answers 401
sign up in MAIN -> portal onboarding -> workspace -> notes with plan quota; second user cannot see the data
plan limit is enforced and explained in the UI
an expired portal token is renewed silently from the live MAIN session; sign-out ends access at once
tampered / garbage portal cookies are refused (and MAIN has no session to renew from)
billing page: owner sees plan and invoices area; billing details stay hidden from plain members

suites.title: pricing page - prices come only from the server catalogue

specs.title: [I04][I05] displayed prices equal the database-backed API (monthly and annual), with computed saving
[I06] annual/monthly switch works with the mouse and the keyboard and exposes its state
seat count changes the displayed total
[I13] a price change in PostgreSQL shows on the page after reload; nothing is cached or hard-coded
[I14] annual billing is disabled (not invented) when a plan has no annual price row
[I15] catalogue unavailable => explicit "unavailable" state, buying disabled, NO fallback prices; Retry recovers
when the server says checkout is not available, purchase buttons are disabled with an explanation
[I12] Enterprise "Contact sales" creates a real inquiry in PostgreSQL (and the honeypot does not)
signed-out visitors who click Buy are sent to sign in and come back to pricing
[I10] signed-in Buy creates a SERVER-SIDE checkout with the database price; the redirect alone activates nothing; a verified webhook does
notes are private by default, searchable and filed in notebooks; a colleague in the same workspace sees none of it
